When Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva walked out of the Federal Police headquarters in Curitiba, Brazil, on November 8, 2019, hundreds of supporters were waiting for him.
Many had been there, on and off, for much of the 580 days he spent behind bars, keeping vigil outside the building and calling out “good morning,” “good afternoon” and “good night” as they defended his innocence and demanded his freedom.
Lula emerged into the crowd and did what he had done best throughout his political life: he gave a speech. “They didn’t imprison a man,” he declared. “They tried to kill an idea. But you can’t kill an idea.”

France is bracing for yet another wave of protests this weekend with authorities racing to prevent a repeat of the kind of violence and riots that hit the nation last week.
French authorities will be launching a massive security operation with some 70,000 police officers deployed across the country over the weekend, according to the interior ministry.
Specialist SWAT units, helicopters, armored vehicles, police dogs and water cannons will all be part of the operation. On top of that, the number of French army soldiers that normally patrol Paris as part of the country’s counter-terrorism measures will be increased to free the police from stationary guard duties.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez issued a stark warning on Friday to anyone looking for trouble, saying the government would be “uncompromising with those who engage in destruction.”

Rome —
A Florida woman died after plunging more than 300 meters (around 1,000 feet) while hiking in the Italian Dolomite mountains, according to police in the northern city of Trentino.
Her death on Saturday was announced late this week after her next of kin were notified, police say.
Michelle Alejandra Rubio-Leiva, who was 36 and from Miami, was on vacation with family members on the Forcella Pordoi trail, a high-altitude site in the Sella group of the Dolomites, when she fell, police told CNN.
The UNESCO World Heritage Site, known for its sweeping views and zig-zag canyon, is only accessible by cable car and reaches 2,848 meters (9,344 feet) at its highest.

item.title: In this border town, a library is trying to preserve a 125-year-old bond between the US and Canada
item.description:

Derby Line, Vermont —
In this border town of about 700 people, you can’t separate the United States and Canada — regardless of politics.
Driving its streets, two things stand out: a downhill funnel to the US-Canada border checkpoint, and a uniquely ornate library that for more than a century has embodied the longstanding bond between the two neighboring allies.
The Haskell Free Library and Opera House opened in 1901 with the US-Canada border running right through the middle of the building, represented by a black line on the floor. Some parts of the library are in Vermont while others are in Quebec, although visitors can use both sides.
On the ground floor there are books in English and French while upstairs there’s a theater where people in the audience can sit in the US with their feet in Canada.

item.title: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda after patient dies
item.description: France on Thursday reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage.

item.title: Strong 7-magnitude earthquake strikes China’s Tibet region
item.description: A strong magnitude 7 earthquake struck China’s Tibet at 10.30 p.m. local time on Thursday, according to the United States Geological Survey (USGS).

item.title: El Salvador sends troops to Haiti to rescue four service members, source says
item.description: El Salvador has deployed troops to Haiti to try to rescue four Salvadoran service members believed to have been captured by Haitian gangs, according to a spokesperson for a UN-authorized multinational security mission in Haiti known as the Gang Suppression Force (GSF).

item.title: Nothing personal between me and Trump, Zelensky tells CNN
item.description: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has told CNN the currently strained relationship between his country and the United States is “not something personal between me and President Trump.”

item.title: Foreign citizen beaten to death during march in South Africa as anti-immigrant tensions flare
item.description: A foreign citizen was beaten to death by a group of around 50 people during a protest march in South Africa’s east coast city of Durban, police said Thursday, as anti-immigrant tensions continue to flare in Africa’s most advanced economy.
